tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

# User arbitrations of the blocking report (verbatim, French)

Arbitrages (rapport bloquant, section 7) :

Q1 : (b). Ajouter à §63 « la destination est utilisable dans l'état d'arrivée ».
Q2 : lecture mixte sur l'état d'arrivée : invariants du noyau sur l'état entier, plus ArenaInv de la nouvelle entrée ; NewArenaBase porte cette lecture.
Q3 : réalisation par des pas du noyau. freeSlot (contrat HandlePool v0.5) marque l'entrée libre et incrémente la génération ; préconditions : droit d'administration, pool vivant, handle valide, aucune feuille de l'entrée à Init (Uninit ou Moved), aucune autorité active dérivée d'une compagne de ce pool sur l'entrée ; aucun effet d'endUse. Deux preuves obligatoires :
  (1) témoin complet depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés : newPool, allocSlot, resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de la valeur vers un local de même forme, unresolve, freeSlot accepté ;
  (2) la mise à jour des métadonnées (état libre, génération) est réalisable par une écriture autorisée sous le droit d'administration.
Q4 : garantie par pool : réécrire D.2, D.3 et D.4(3) sur les compagnes du pool du slot ; les pools imbriqués restent permis ; I1 et les garanties du noyau restent prouvées sur l'état entier.
Q5 : la validation du handle précède le contrôle du droit : fail dans les deux cas.
Q6 : réécrire §86 s4 : « La réémission ne modifie ni les octets ni l'état d'initialisation. Une lecture reste soumise aux conditions ordinaires du modèle mémoire, notamment Init, aux droits d'accès et à la validité de représentation pour le type demandé. La Spec 4 déterminera les obligations de construction et de typage des valeurs réémises. »
Q7 : restreindre §78.3 aux ancres du sous-arbre strict de internal qui couvrent une feuille du stockage administré ; prouver que la clause découle de §78.2 et de I3 (lecture Q9), et l'équivalence de reset avec sa séquence du noyau dans les deux sens.
Q8 : ajouter à §47 : le graphe de possession des statiques est acyclique.
Q9 et Q26 : « valide » = active. §69.2 : endUse est rejeté si une autorité détenue par place a un descendant actif détenu ailleurs.
Q10 : (a).
Q11 : (a) fail ; (b) reject ; (c) reject ; (d) mark exige AdminRight ; (e) grow suit le détenteur actuel du bloc ; (f) fail avant le contrôle du droit (contrat DS-v2).
Q12 : avec le nouveau freeSlot, un handle d'entrée libre est périmé : fail.
Q13 : §71.2 inchangé ; préciser au §36 que MetaRight vise la création ou le recyclage d'autorités sur un stockage existant, pas la création d'une allocation fraîche par alloc ; la concurrence entre appels relève de la spec 2.
Q14 : « opérations d'accès » = O9–O11 ; le préciser au §59.
Q15 : restreindre §40 aux emplacements racines utilisables, comme §49.7.
Q16 : définir I5 : toute feuille épinglée appartient à un emplacement utilisable.
Q17 : lecture actuelle.
Q18 : région dont toutes les feuilles sont de taille nulle : base et provenance de l'allocation de l'ancre effective, comme la région vide.
Q19 : H31a : le jumeau à plusieurs pas (conjonct 5) est accepté.
Q20 : non bloquants (classés).
Q21 : pour chaque cas dont le verdict attendu change, conserver le verdict historique, sa justification et le nouveau verdict fondé sur la v0.1 (tableau dans la description de PR) :
  - H21, H50, H51 : nouveau verdict = verdict obtenu ;
  - H49 : conservé comme test de régression, verdict = verdict obtenu, blocage résiduel documenté (décision NoLock) ; exception explicite : le reset rejeté de H49 est dispensé de jumeau positif ;
  - H16 classé spec 3 ; W2 et W3 : les variantes deviennent les cas ; MM2-H H01 : la variante devient le jumeau ; H10 : l'accès sort de l'allocation ; W1 : la valeur est retirée avant freeSlot.
Q22 : non bloquants (frontières ouvertes de la spec) ; exitRoots retenu comme réalisation de référence.
Q23 : lectures dont un témoin du rapport change un verdict :
  - B#1, B#15, B#33, SP-A4, machine S1 et S2 : lectures actuelles conservées (B#15 imposée par Q9) ;
  - B#28 : remplacée par Q9 ;
  - B#45 : remplacée : chaque pin crée une obligation d'épinglage d'identité fraîche ; une feuille est épinglée tant qu'une obligation active la couvre ; unpin désigne une obligation et ne lève qu'elle ; K.ExternalDone porte sur cette obligation ;
  - H-R5 : sans objet ; DS-R1 à DS-R13 : tranchées par Q11, Q27 et Q28.
  Les lectures sans témoin de différence sont conservées.
Q24 : le fournisseur doit être un emplacement utilisable (§71.2).
Q25 : (b).
Q27 : (a).
Q28 : (c) fail (une pile morte invalide ses marques).

Spec : ne pas modifier `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. Créer `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` à partir de la v0, avec les amendements Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9/Q26, Q13, Q14, Q15, Q16, Q18, Q24 et B#45 (§74, §75), en anglais ; en-tête : « Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated », suivi de la liste des clauses modifiées. Commit séparé `docs(specs): add memory model v0.1 corrective candidate`. La reconstruction suit la v0.1.
Contrats locaux : HandlePool v0.5 (Q3, Q4, Q5, Q12) et DS-v2 (Q11, Q27, Q28), changements listés dans la description de PR.
Preuves : refaire celles qui sont touchées ; les garanties de Q1, Q3, Q7 et B#45 sont démontrées sur les états atteignables du contrat, sans hypothèse supplémentaire non normative ; tout échec de preuve est rapporté, jamais contourné. Ouvrir la PR si la condition du brief est remplie.

## Follow-up answers (verbatim, French)

Q9 (suite) : règle unifiée. endUse et free sont rejetés si une autorité qu'ils désactivent — détenue par un emplacement qui meurt, stockage possédé transitivement compris, ou racine d'un stockage libéré — a un descendant actif, quelle que soit son empreinte, que le même pas ne désactive pas. Les cas (1) et (2) sont donc rejetés. La sortie de cadre garde son ré-ancrage, et rejette si aucune origine survivante n'existe (inchangé). I2 au sens « origine active » tient après chaque pas.

Q3 (suite) : remplace Q17. Dans §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3, sont exemptées des contrôles « autorité dérivée active couvrant depuis l'extérieur » les autorités par lesquelles le pas exerce son droit Modify : l'autorité exerçable qui fonde le droit et sa chaîne d'origines (pour le pool : entrée, compagne, internal et ses origines). Les autres autorités actives restent contrôlées. Le témoin Q3 (1) devient : resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de l'entrée vers un local, unresolve, freeSlot accepté, y compris avec internal dérivé. W1 suit le même chemin. Réévaluer W2 sous cette lecture. Ajouter §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3 aux amendements de la v0.1.

(Cases (1) and (2) above refer to: (1) endUse(p) where p owns an allocation q holding a stored authority a, the frame holding b derived from a over another static; (2) free(p) with an empty-footprint derivative of p's root held by the frame.)

## Second follow-up answers (verbatim, French), after the library phase

HandlePool v0.5, freeSlot : remplacer la condition par « aucune autorité active, descendante stricte de internal de ce pool, ne couvre l'entrée ». Le ré-ancrage sur internal (§73) est alors couvert, et la garantie reste par pool : un pool imbriqué dans une entrée bloque la libération de cette entrée, alors que les autorités du pool parent ne bloquent pas les freeSlot du pool imbriqué, puisqu'elles sont des ancêtres de son internal et non des descendantes. pool_no_stale_access doit tenir sous cette règle.

DataStack :
- DS-R1 : toute cellule de position ≥ m.top (lecture la plus stricte) ;
- DS-R4 : grow avec extra = 0 est ok (réémission en place de la même région) ;
- DS-R3 : rewind sur un indice de pile inexistant donne fail, comme une marque invalide (cohérent avec Q5 et Q28).

Q5 : oui, étendre à freeSlot. La validation du handle précède le contrôle du droit : le handle d'un pool mort donne fail.

## Context

## Hard rules (in addition to AGENTS.md)

- No `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide`, `noncomputable`, `set_option`. No warnings.
- Every constant's axioms must be within {propext, Quot.sound}. `Classical.choice` is NOT allowed. Avoid
  `Classical`, `by_contra` on non-decidable props, `Decidable.byContradiction` on classical instances,
  `simp` lemmas that pull `Classical.choice` (check if unsure with `#print axioms` in a scratch file
  under `SP/`).
- Every def/theorem docstring cites the clause it formalizes (`§63.9`, `§69.2`, ...). Module headers that
  name the spec file must name `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`.
- Everything in English. Do not commit; do not touch git state (no stash, checkout, reset).
- Never weaken a statement, never add an unjustified hypothesis, never change a definition to make a
  proof go through. If a proof is stuck on a goal you believe false, build a concrete counterexample
  (a `decide`-checked state) if you can, stop and report the goal state.
- New helper lemmas you add to a file that other agents do not own must be `private` or carry a
  file-specific prefix, so that two files never define the same public name.

## Fixed design (decided by the orchestrator; do not deviate, report instead)

D1 Pinning obligations (v0.1 §74, §75; arbitration Q23 B#45).
  - In `Basic.lean`, add
    `structure PinOb where place : Nat; leaves : List Nat; active : Bool` (deriving DecidableEq, Repr):
    a dynamic pinning obligation, its identity being its index in `S3.pins`.
  - Replace the field `S3.pin : Nat → Bool` by `pins : List PinOb`.
  - Define `S3.pin (s : S3) (l : Nat) : Bool := s.pins.any fun o => o.active && o.leaves.contains l`
    (a leaf is dynamically pinned while an active obligation covers it), so that existing uses
    `s.pin l = false` keep their meaning.
  - `pinEff s p := { s with pins := s.pins ++ [⟨p, footprint s.P p, true⟩] }` (fresh identity = index).
  - `unpin` takes an obligation identity `o`. Effect: obligation `o` becomes inactive, nothing else changes.
    `UnpinPre k s o`: obligation `o` exists and is active; its place is usable; `HasRight s .modify place`;
    `k.ExternalDone o`.
  - `K.ExternalDone : Nat → Prop` keeps its type; it now applies to obligation identities (fix docstring).
  - `enterEff`, `allocEff`, `S3.init` no longer touch pins (`S3.init`: `pins := []`).
  - `PinPre` unchanged.
D2 Grounding of a right (v0.1 §63.4, §69.2, §70.3; follow-up answer "Q3 (suite)").
  - `Grounds (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q g : Nat) : Prop :=`
    `g ∈ List.range s.A.length ∧ s.ExercisableAt g m ∧ ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s g l) m`

  - `RightChain (s : S3) (g j : Nat) : Prop := j = g ∨ j ∈ s.ancs g` (`ancs` = strict ancestors).

  - New field `dstUsableAfter : (transferEff s src dst).Usable dst` (v0.1 §63.9).

  - `access` becomes: `∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify p g ∧`

  - New field `keptDesc : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active a →`

# Kernel phase report (wf_a43949df-c92, committed as 44df9a0)

## Stage 1 definitions
status: done

Stage 1 is done. D1–D10 are implemented in Basic, Ops, Invariants, Lemmas and Preserve/Common under formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/. `cd formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake build Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.Common` succeeds with no warnings. Each of the five files also compiles silently with `lake env lean`. The grep for sorry/admit/native_decide/axiom/noncomputable/set_option finds nothing in these files. I ran a scratch meta-check (scratchpad/stage1/AllAx.lean) over all 1359 constants of the five modules: every one depends only on propext and Quot.sound, with no Classical.choice.

Spec passages read: v0.1 §38–§57, §58–§75 and the header; arbitration.md, including the follow-up answers Q9 and Q3.

What changed:
- **D1 (§74, §75; B#45)**
  - New `PinOb`. The `S3.pin` field is replaced by `pins : List PinOb`, with `def S3.pin` derived from it, so `s.pin l = false` keeps its meaning.
  - `pinEff s p` appends the obligation `⟨p, footprint s.P p, true⟩`.
  - New `unpinEff s o` deactivates only obligation `o` (via `List.modify`; every other field stays the same by rfl).
  - `UnpinPre k s o` has four fields: obligation `o` exists and is active; its place is usable; `HasRight .modify` on that place; `k.ExternalDone o`.
  - `UnpinStep k o` and `KStep.unpin {o}` are updated.
  - `enterEff` and `allocEff` no longer touch pins (`enterEff` sets `pins := s.pins`). `S3.init` has `pins := []`.
  - The `K` docstring now says `ExternalDone` is applied to obligation identities.
- **D2:** `Grounds` and `RightChain` are added after `HasRight`, with `Decidable` instances.
- **D3:** `TransferPre.noOutsideDerived` takes the ∃ g form, and the new field `dstUsableAfter` covers §63.9.
- **D4 / D5:** `EndUsePre.access` and `FreePre.access` take the ∃ g form with `RightChain ∨ ...AccessOK`. Each gets a new `keptDesc` field for the last sentence of §69.2 and §70.3.
- **D6:** new `AllocStatic.providerUsable`.
- **D7:** new `DerivePre.chainActive`.
- **D8:** `I2` gets the conjunct `(y.active = true → x.active = true)`.
- **D9:** `I5 k s` is defined and is not part of `KInv`.
- **D10:** the `StaticsOK` docstring now cites §47 and §49.
- **Docstrings and headers:** all `Decidable` instances are updated for the new fields. Module headers now cite `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`. The `KAux` docstring now says it is not a clause of §57 (D11 wording), because no later stage can edit Common.lean.

Examples in Invariants.lean:
- New state `s4 := pinEff s0 0`.
- `UnpinPre K0 s4 0` holds; `¬ UnpinPre K0 s0 0` (no obligation exists); `¬ EndUsePre K0 s4 0` (the leaf is pinned).
- A §75 witness: with two obligations on leaf 0, unpinning obligation 0 leaves the leaf pinned, while unpinning the only obligation unpins it.
- The §63.8 example is restated with the new §63.4 form plus the §63.9 conjunct.
- All existing `decide` examples still pass with the new fields: TransferPre, EndUsePre, FreePre, AllocStatic and DerivePre.

New general lemmas in Lemmas.lean:
- `mem_chain`.
- `hasRight_iff_grounds` (HasRight ↔ ∃ g, Grounds).
- I2 accessors: `I2.origin_active`, `I2.ancs_active_lt`, `I2.ancs_active` (under I2, every authority in the origin chain of an active authority is active).
- Pinning lemmas:
  - `S3.pin_iff`, `S3.pin_congr`;
  - `pin_pinEff`;
  - `pins_unpinEff`, `pin_unpinEff_iff`, `pin_of_pin_unpinEff`;
  - one `pins_*Eff` lemma per pin-free effect: derive, split, release, transfer, depend, store, enter, exit, write3, endUse, free, alloc.
- One private helper, `getElem?_modify'`. The core `List.getElem?_modify` depends on Classical.choice, so I proved my own version.

Changed proofs: `SameSkel.i2` now carries the active conjunct. `addAuth_preserves` gained the hypothesis `hxa : x.active = true`. That hypothesis comes from the spec (§60.1 and §61.1 require the source to be active), and the proof cannot work without it once I2 changes: a `derive` with an empty region from an inactive source would break I2. The lemma has no users outside Lemmas.lean.

Not done: per the brief, I did not run the full build; the Access stage-2 files (Preserve/*), Main.lean and modules outside Access/ are expected to fail until later stages run. Line numbers for every declaration are in `changed`; the stage-2 changes needed, the git-state note and the §63.4/§69.2/§70.3 reading are in `open`.

Open:
- Interface changes stage 2 must absorb (they are expected, not blockers): `pinEff` now takes 2 arguments (no Bool), and `unpin` uses the new `unpinEff s o`. Small.lean's `pinEff_preserves_*` lemmas need `pinEff s p` and `unpinEff s o`; both effects change only `pins`, and every other field is unchanged by rfl. `I2` has a 4th conjunct, which affects `Alloc.i2`, the private `addAuth_i2` and `release_preserves_i2` in DeriveSplitRelease.lean, and the `obtain ⟨x₁, hx₁, hm, hsub⟩` at EndFree.lean:307. Structures with new fields break positional destructuring: DerivePre (+chainActive, 3rd field), TransferPre (§63.4 field reshaped, +dstUsableAfter last), EndUsePre and FreePre (access reshaped, +keptDesc after access), AllocStatic (+providerUsable before providerInit).
- Reading in the fixed design D3–D5 (for the reviewer, not a deviation): §63.4, §69.2 and §70.3 exempt 'the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain'. The operations' signatures do not name which authority the step exercises, so the formalization uses `∃ g, Grounds ... ∧ ...`. When several authorities ground the right, the step is accepted if any one of them exempts every outsider. The spec text (singular 'the authority') does not settle this choice.
- I5 (D9) is defined; the reachability theorem belongs to stage 3. A sketch suggests I5 is inductive under KInv (WF3 parts share owner and death; §63.9, §69.4, §70.4 and §73.3 each block the step that would strand a pinned leaf), so no new auxiliary appears necessary. I did not prove this.
- Git state: `formal/Ern/Corpus/MM2H.lean` is modified in the working tree (mtime 08:18:11). I never touched it, and the git status at session start was clean, so another process changed it.

## Review findings
- minor formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Ops.lean:307 (TransferPre.noOutsideDerived); spec §63.4 of specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md: No formalization error: the field matches D3 and §63.4 word for word. This is an observation about the spec. On any state satisfying I1, the v0.1 §63.4 check with its exemption is already implied by §63.1 (srcRight). Every active authority that covers a source leaf is either the grounding authority, one of its origins, or a descendant (which would cancel the grounding authority's effective Modify), or it is unrelated to the grounding authority (I1 then forces both modes to Observe). So 'Other active authorities remain subject to this check' never rejects anything on reachable states, and no witness can show §63.4 rejecting a transfer from a reachable state. The same does not hold for §69.2 and §70.3, because their ending and freed leaves include owned storage outside the footprint of `place`. No change is requested. This is information for whoever writes witness theorems (D12) or re-evaluates W2 (follow-up Q3). EVIDENCE: Scratch proof /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref/v01/review-defs/Vacuous.lean: `theorem noOutsideDerived_of_grounds {s : S3} (h1 : I1 s) {src g : Nat} (hg : Grounds s .modify src g) (j : Nat) (hj : ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) : RightChain s g j`. `cd formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean <file>` prints `'noOutsideDerived_of_grounds' depends on axioms: [propext, Quot.sound]`. Together with `hasRight_iff_grounds`, this gives srcRight ∧ I1 → noOutsideDerived. Spec §63.4: "No active derived authority held outside `source` covers a source leaf, except ... the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain. Other active authorities remain subject to this check."
- minor formal/Ern/Corpus/MM2H.lean (outside the reviewed directory): The working tree has an uncommitted change to a Corpus module. The kernel brief forbids touching Corpus in this phase. The change implements arbitration Q21: the H01 twin is replaced by its variant, and H10_inside and h10out are removed. These are not D1-D11 items. I cannot tell whether stage 1 made this change or a separate corpus workflow did. If stage 1 made it, it is out of scope; otherwise disregard this finding. EVIDENCE: `git status --short` lists ` M formal/Ern/Corpus/MM2H.lean` alongside the five stage-1 files. The file's mtime is Nov 6 08:18:11, inside the stage-1 window (Ops.lean 08:18:46, Basic.lean 08:20:43). Kernel brief: "Modules outside `MemoryModel/Access/` (Arena, Refinement, RefinementArena, Lib, Corpus) will be broken during this phase; do not touch them." Diff excerpt: `-theorem H10_inside : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ¬ Derive h10src h10out ∧` and `-theorem H01_twin_variant :`.
- minor formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Invariants.lean:115 (def I5; statement fixed by brief D9): I5 is stronger than §57. §57 talks only about pinned leaves. The formal I5 quantifies over every index l with K.Pinned l, so it also asserts that K.Pinned designates only existing leaves of usable places. Two kinds of K satisfy §57's I5 at the start but fail the formal one: a K that pins a non-leaf place, and a K that pins a leaf identity that alloc creates later. The planned I5 reachability theorem takes `I5 k (S3.init statics)` as hypothesis, so it says nothing for those K, which narrows its domain. Accepted programs do not change, because every pin check reads only leaves. Cause: formalization error, inherited from D9's statement. EVIDENCE: Spec §57: "I5: every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place." Lean checks in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref/v01/review-defs/ConsequencesI5.lean (`lake env lean`, exit 0). The leaf-restricted reading `I5leaf KN (S3.init stN)` (∀ l < |P|, isLeaf l → pinned → ∃ usable q, l ∈ footprint q) is true by decide. `¬ I5 KN (S3.init stN)` is proved. (2) Later-created leaf: KF.Pinned l := l = 3 with the 3-static example state s0. `I5leaf KF s0` holds; `¬ I5 KF s0` is proved. After `alloc` (s2, place 3 owned by place 1), `I5leaf KF s2` holds, and both `¬ FreePre KF s2 3 0` and `¬ EndUsePre KF s2 1` are decided. So §57's I5 is kept for this K, yet the formal hypothesis excludes it.
- minor formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Ops.lean:307 (TransferPre.noOutsideDerived; same structure in EndUsePre.access and FreePre.access for the leaves of `place`): This is a consequence of the amendment, not a formalization error: the formalization follows §63.4. With the exemption, the remaining §63.4 check can never reject in a state satisfying I1, so in every KInv state it follows from §63.1's source right. In reachable states, v0.1 `transfer` therefore accepts exactly as if the third sentence of §63.4 and its exemption were not there. Arbitration Q3 (suite) says "Les autres autorités actives restent contrôlées", but for transfer that control never rejects anything. For endUse and free, the remaining check still matters only for the leaves of storage that dies with `place`. EVIDENCE: Spec §63.4: "... except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `source`: the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain. Other active authorities remain subject to this check." Lean proof in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref/v01/review-defs/TransferExemptVacuous.lean, checked with `lake env lean` (exit 0): `review_noOutside_of_right : I1 s → HasRight s .modify src → ∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify src g ∧ ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ActiveDerivedOutside s src j → RightChain s g j`. Output: "'review_noOutside_of_right' depends on axioms: [propext, Quot.sound]". Proof idea: an active j covering a source leaf l either is a descendant of g, which contradicts effective(g,l)=Modify (§43 case 3/4), or is unrelated to g, which contradicts I1 because g's own mode is Modify. ## Stage 1 fix
status: done

I checked all four findings against the v0.1 text, the kernel brief and the arbitration file. Open:

status: done

I re-proved formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Preserve/Small.lean against the v0.1 definitions. `cd formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean Ern/MemoryModel/Access/Preserve/Small.lean` reports no errors and no warnings. **I2 with an active origin.** For depend, read, write, writeShared and store, the KInv proofs compiled unchanged. **I5 lemmas.** None of the seven needs an invariant hypothesis on `s`:

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

# II. Values, Allocations, and Access Representation

A value, a place, and a means of access are three distinct notions. The abstract machine distinguishes their existence from their permissions and temporal validity.

## 8. Values and Storage Identity

A **value** is semantic content; a **place** is a portion of storage capable of containing that content; a **means of access** allows a place to be designated under certain conditions.

**Values without intrinsic identity (MVS):** A value has no intrinsic identity. Identity belongs to storage or to a resource designated by the value, not to the value itself. Copying a value, transferring an authority, and accessing a place are semantically distinct operations. The access, consumption, and transfer rules within this model are defined in the following sections; copyability and its typing belong to the appropriate specifications.

## 9. Abstract Allocations and Admissible State

An abstract allocation has at least:

- a **unique identity** within the abstract execution;
- an **address space**;
- a **base address**;
- an **extent** expressed in bytes;
- a strictly positive, power-of-two **alignment** satisfied by its base;
- a **live** or **dead** state;
- abstract offset-indexable storage made up of abstract bytes;
- if deallocatable, **deallocation-authority** conditions.

An abstract allocation does not necessarily correspond to a library allocator call. The kernel also represents storage with static or automatic duration, whose particular rules will be defined later.

**Disjointness of live allocations:** Two distinct live abstract allocations in the **same address space** occupy **disjoint** address ranges. Ranges are half-open: `[base, base + size)`. Two disjoint ranges have an empty intersection. Thus, a zero-sized range overlaps no other range.

**Allocation alignment:** Every **registered** abstract allocation, live or dead, has a strictly positive power-of-two alignment; its base is a multiple of that alignment. Valid alignment is a property of admissible states, not merely a creation-time check.

Subplaces returned by an arena or a data stack within an allocation are **not automatically new abstract allocations**: they may share its identity and provenance. The abstract machine is *flat*: it introduces no parent–child hierarchy of allocations.

The base and extent are modeled over natural numbers in this kernel. Constraints on address width, actually available spaces, and possible overflow of hardware representations are reserved for conversion, layout, and ABI rules; they are not implicitly proved by this mathematical abstraction.

**Admissible state and domain:** The abstract state contains registered allocations and a freshness discipline. **Freshness requires that a newly assigned identity has never been assigned before**, even to an allocation that has since died. A monotonically increasing counter is one possible representation, not a language requirement.

Admissible states jointly satisfy:

- **Well-formedness of identities and freshness:** the preceding discipline is consistent with the registered allocations;
- **Disjointness of live allocations:** two distinct live allocations in the same address space do not overlap;
- **Alignment:** every registered allocation, live or dead, has valid alignment and an aligned base.

Normative memory semantics applies to **admissible states**, namely those satisfying these three properties. An empty state is an admissible initial state and allows reachability proofs; it is **not the only admissible initial state**. An initial configuration supplied by the environment or interoperability may be admissible if it satisfies the required invariants. Establishing such conformity belongs to the applicable initialization or interoperability contract.

**Fundamental distinction:** Well-formedness, disjointness, and alignment, as invariants of admissible states, determine the **domain** of the semantics. Their violation in an arbitrary state outside that domain **is not, by itself, a new operational obligation whose violation would be classified as UB**. Relations in a Lean model may nevertheless be mathematically total on such states; their outcomes do not bind the language specification outside the admissible domain.

**Raw creation:** In an admissible state, creation of a live allocation requires a fresh identity, valid alignment, a correctly aligned base, and no overlap with any distinct live allocation in the same space. These conditions are **operation** preconditions; their violation by an unsafe raw operation constitutes UB. They are distinct from domain invariants even when one guarantees some of them. Actual resource reservation may additionally fail in a defined manner according to the allocator contract; that case is not equated with a violation of a raw-operation precondition.

The abstract machine does not mandate a physical allocation table, `next` counter, or liveness flags at runtime; these are semantic and formalization tools.

## 10. Bytes and Initialization

This kernel considers **8-bit bytes**, whose initialized value ranges from 0 to 255.

An abstract byte is either:

- **uninitialized**;
- **initialized**, with a byte value and optional provenance information.

State is tracked **per byte** to permit partially initialized allocations. In this kernel, the provenance component can be represented by an optional allocation identity; this representation may be enriched by the access discipline. This component is **semantic** information: its existence does not imply a provenance tag physically stored in every byte.

Stored provenance comes from the **value and its representation being written**, not automatically from the provenance of the means of access used to perform the write. Rules for propagation of provenance during byte copies and reinterpretations are not yet fixed.

The initial state of a **newly created raw allocation** is wholly uninitialized. Initializing static values or constructing initialized objects are additional operations; it does not follow that all observable static storage starts uninitialized.

“All required bytes are initialized” and “these bytes represent a valid value of type T” are two different properties. Constraints on invalid representations, padding bytes, and type alignment will be specified by the corresponding specifications.

## 11. Abstract Physical Places

A place designates a portion of an allocation's storage. In the minimal kernel, it is defined by that allocation's identity, an offset, and a length. Typed interpretations, subplaces, and fine-grained permissions may extend this representation.

Resolution of a means of access to a place must be explicitly defined. It is **partial**: a means of access produces a place only if provenance identifies a **registered allocation (live or dead)** and the address range is spatially contained within it. Producing a resolved place does not, by itself, prove the right to read or write: liveness, initialization, authority, type, alignment, and concurrency are established separately by the applicable rules.

## 12. Accesses, Addresses, and Provenance

A means of access conceptually contains:

- an **address**;
- **provenance** identifying the designated allocation;
- an **extent** or access length;
- an **access authority**;
- any other information necessary for its validity.

In the elementary memory machine, provenance identifies the allocation; the access discipline in Part IV and following may associate additional constraints with it. **Access authority** (read, write, etc.) is distinct from **deallocation authority**.

Resolution uses provenance, **never simply selecting an allocation at the requested numerical address**. A reused address does not validate an old means of access.

In the abstract memory machine of Parts II and III, elementary read/write authority is ordered `read ≤ write`; this elementary authority does not replace the discipline of `Observe` and `Modify` modes defined below. In this simplified model, the elementary read-authority condition excludes no access carrying either of those two authorities; substantive rules for observation, modification, and revocation belong to the access discipline. An authority may later become state-dependent and be invalidated.

# III. Memory Machine: Accesses and Byte Transitions

The following relations describe effects on allocations and bytes, independently of the higher-level permissions subsequently established by the authority discipline.

## 13. Allocation Identity and Address Reuse

Each creation of an abstract allocation assigns an identity **never reused** during the abstract execution. A dead allocation may remain registered for reasoning purposes without becoming live again.

The same numerical address may be reused after the previous storage has been freed. Such reuse never restores the rights or validity of an access carrying the old allocation's provenance.

Creating a new allocation does not change pre-existing allocations; read/write/deallocation operations do not create fresh identities unless an explicit later rule provides otherwise.

## 14. Restrictive Derivation of Means of Access

A **restrictive derivation** of a means of access:

- preserves the source allocation's provenance;
- designates a **subrange** of the source access;
- confers no authority greater than that permitted by the source.

In the elementary memory machine, provenance has **allocation granularity**, not field or subrange granularity. Finer-grained rights restrictions are determined by the authority discipline defined in Part IV and following.

A valid restrictive derivation is not necessarily the only way to form an address or create a means of access. A safe abstraction may, through mechanisms and invariants yet to be defined, provide new rights to disjoint places; **the creation of rights is not reducible to restrictive derivation**.

Forming an address or a means of access is distinct from **using** it. Merely forming an out-of-bounds address is not automatically classified as UB; precise formation and conversion restrictions remain open in Section 19.

## 15. Typed Reads and Validity Conditions

For an allocation with base `b` and size `s`, an access with address `a` and length `n` is **spatially contained** when `b ≤ a` and `a + n ≤ b + s`. The corresponding ranges are `[a, a+n)` and `[b, b+s)`.

A typed read requires all applicable conditions:

1. provenance resolves to a **live** allocation;
2. the access is **spatially contained** in that allocation;
3. the bytes **required** for the representation being read are initialized;
4. that representation is valid for the read type;
5. read authority is valid;
6. the alignment constraints of the read type are satisfied;
7. concurrency rules are satisfied.

For a zero-length range, the spatial condition permits any address in `[b, b+s]` and requires no initialized bytes. **This does not automatically permit every zero-length typed read**: the operation remains subject to all its other conditions.

Violation of a safety obligation of an **unsafe raw** read constitutes UB. A safe read interface must establish the condition or report a defined failure before the dangerous operation.

Conditions 4, 6, and 7 are not concretely defined by this kernel; they remain explicit, parameterizable obligations. The choice of how to establish them (static proof, genuinely executable dynamic check, abstraction contract) remains open, subject to Section 4. Thus, kernel theorems alone do not prove the complete validity of an ERN typed read.

## 16. Typed Writes and Preservation of the Memory Frame

A typed write requires all applicable conditions:

1. provenance resolves to a **live** allocation;
2. the place is **spatially contained** as specified in Section 15;
3. write authority is valid;
4. the value and its representation are admissible for the type being written;
5. alignment constraints are satisfied;
6. concurrency rules are satisfied.

A valid write replaces the bytes of the written range **byte by byte** with the supplied representation and its provenance information, then marks the affected bytes initialized. It may initialize a previously uninitialized range. Provenance of the written bytes follows from the representation of the value written, not merely from the provenance of the means of access.

Bytes in other allocations and bytes outside the written range in the target allocation remain unchanged; allocation identity and the allocation counter are unaffected. The consequences of replacement for a pre-existing typed value remain to be determined.

Conditions 4, 5, and 6 are not concretely defined by this kernel; they remain explicit, parameterizable obligations. A raw write violating a safety obligation is UB; a safe interface must prevent it or produce a defined failure.

**Read-after-write and non-interference:** A valid write initializes the bytes of the written range. In the absence of an intervening write or invalidation, **every valid raw byte read of a subrange contained in the written range**, including the entire range, returns exactly the corresponding subsequence of the written contents, including abstract provenance information, subject to the other read conditions. A valid write changes neither the result of a valid read of another allocation nor that of a range disjoint from the written range. These properties concern abstract bytes and do not prejudge the reconstruction of a typed value.

## 17. Deallocation and Invalidation of Old Accesses

Successful raw deallocation requires:

1. an abstract allocation that is **live** and deallocatable;
2. **deallocation authority compatible** with that required by the allocation.

Compatibility is a semantic relation; it does not necessarily require the two allocator handles to have numerically identical identities, and it is distinct from access provenance.

Successful deallocation ends the allocation's validity. Accesses carrying its provenance can no longer read or write that old storage. An attempted double deallocation through the raw operation violates a safety obligation and constitutes UB. A safe abstraction that detects an incompatible attempt before performing a dangerous operation may produce a defined failure; this does not require a universal checked-deallocation primitive.

In the elementary memory machine, compatibility is defined between the presented authority and the recorded deallocation token. A library allocator may additionally impose constraints depending on its own state; these do not change the minimal signature of the kernel's compatibility relation.

**Validity of derived rights:** The logical invalidation of an object inside an allocation that is still live—for example, a block following an arena reset—is governed by the authorities, anchors, and end-of-use rules in Parts IV through XIV. It does not change the two elementary deallocation conditions in Section 17.

## 18. Boundary with Concurrency and Data Races

**A *data race* is UB; no execution of safe code can cause one.** This section establishes that guarantee and its interface with the concurrency model, without purporting to define concurrent events and orderings by itself.

A *data race* involves conflicting accesses to overlapping memory ranges from concurrent execution contexts, at least one of which is a write and at least one of which is non-atomic, when the ordering relations required by the concurrency model do not order them sufficiently. This criterion becomes fully operational only with the event and synchronization semantics of Spec 2.

**Normative boundary:** Spec 2 determines, in particular, the exact definitions of events, conflicts, *happens-before*, atomic operations, and memory orders. The elementary memory machine does not claim that a local access check is sufficient to prove the absence of data races.

## 19. Address Conversions and Provenance: Open Boundary

ERN must distinguish:

1. address calculation that preserves valid provenance;
2. extraction of a numerical address representation;
3. reconstruction of a means of access from an integer;
4. external address spaces and accesses, particularly MMIO;
5. representation transformations, particularly tagged pointers and C interoperability.

None of these conversions may allow safe code to fabricate dangerous access authority.

**Undecided:** exposed provenance, strict provenance, or another model; exact rules for integer–pointer conversions, tagged pointers, and propagation through representation copies. These conversions require a separate definition before any guarantee about reconstructing an access from an integer representation; they are not settled by the simplified provenance of Section 12 alone.

---

## 20. Relational Semantics and Outcomes

**State-domain conditions**, **operation-specific obligations**, **the effect of a valid operation**, and **semantic outcome** must be distinguished.

### 20.1 — Normative Transition Relations

Raw memory-model operations are interpreted by **transition relations**. Their role is to determine the semantic outcome without assuming that all their obligations can be computed at runtime. Operation names are semantic designations independent of any particular implementation or formalization.

In an **admissible** state:

- a raw operation satisfying all applicable obligations has a defined `ok` outcome with the specified effect;
- violation of a safety obligation of that operation produces a `ub` outcome (Section 6), **including when the obligation is static**;
- a `ub` transition does not supply a new ordinary state reusable as a valid step.

Memory-machine relations may be deterministic and mathematically total even when certain obligations are not constructively decidable. A classical proof of totality is not a runtime requirement. Modeling a defined failure of resource reservation belongs to the allocator contract: it does not change the classification of violations of safety obligations of raw operations.

### 20.2 — Read Values and Effects of Other Operations

A valid **byte read** does not modify memory state; its `ok` outcome supplies the sequence of abstract bytes actually read, including provenance. A raw typed read must additionally satisfy type, alignment, and concurrency obligations and subsequent value-reconstruction rules. Unlike operations that only transition the state, a read supplies a value together with its successful outcome.

A valid **write** updates its range according to Section 16. A valid **deallocation** ends allocation liveness according to Section 17. A valid **allocation** creates a fresh identity and its storage according to Sections 9, 10, and 13. Non-interference, invalidation, and invariant-preservation properties apply to their `ok` transitions.

### 20.3 — Parametric Obligations and Executions

Read and write obligations not yet concretely defined are **explicit predicates** of the semantic context: they are not tacitly replaced by `True`.

The formalization may distinguish a component with an executable decision procedure from a component whose satisfaction is established by static reasoning or by contract. **This decomposition remains parametric and does not universally prescribe a strategy for each requirement.** It does not permit concurrent safety to be reduced to a simple local test.

A normative relation requires **no decision instance** for these predicates to be stated. A computable function may require a decision instance for conditions it evaluates. Obligations and the deallocation-compatibility relation are fixed as **parameters of an execution's context**; obligation predicates may nevertheless depend on the state and operation. The minimal compatibility relation of Section 17 concerns the presented authority and the deallocation token; additional state-dependent contracts belong to the relevant abstraction.

/-!
# Elementary memory machine (spec v0, Parts II–III, §8–§20)

Source: `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. Citations: `§N.k` is numbered item `k`
of section `N`; `§N ¶p` is the `p`-th paragraph of section `N`, a list belonging to the
paragraph that introduces it.

* State, allocations, bytes, places and accesses (§9–§12).
* Effects of valid operations: `State.write`, `State.dealloc`, `State.alloc`.
* Raw operations as transition relations with `ok`/`ub` outcomes, stated on every state
  (§20.1): `ReadStep`, `WriteStep`, `DeallocStep`, `AllocStep`. Typed reads and writes carry
  a type argument of an opaque type `Ty`; their unspecified obligations are explicit
  parameters split into a decidable part `dec` and a static part `stat` (§20.3).
* Interpreters `read`, `write`, `dealloc`, `alloc`, computable, with the static part as a
  proof argument (§20.3 ¶3), agreeing with the relations in both directions.
* Executions `Exec` (sequences of `ok` steps) from any initial state (§9 ¶9).
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Machine

/-! ## State and accesses (Part II) -/

/-- Elementary access authority of a means of access (§12 ¶1, §12 ¶4). -/
inductive Auth where
  | read
  | write
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The elementary authority order `read ≤ write`, reflexive (§12 ¶4). -/
instance : LE Auth := ⟨fun a b => a = .read ∨ b = .write⟩

/-- The elementary authority order is decidable (§12 ¶4). -/
instance (a b : Auth) : Decidable (a ≤ b) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (a = .read ∨ b = .write))

/-- Abstract byte: uninitialized, or initialized with an 8-bit value and an optional
provenance represented by an allocation identity (§10 ¶1–¶3). -/
inductive AByte where
  | uninit
  | init (val : UInt8) (prov : Option Nat)
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- Abstract allocation (§9 ¶1). Its identity is its key in `State.allocs`. `bytes` is
indexed by offset from `base`; offsets outside `[0, size)` are reached by no permitted
access (`Spatial`). `freeAuth = some d` records the deallocation token `d` of a
deallocatable allocation (§9 ¶1 b8, §17 ¶4); `none` marks a non-deallocatable one. -/
structure Alloc where
  space : Nat
  base : Nat
  size : Nat
  align : Nat
  live : Bool
  bytes : Nat → AByte
  freeAuth : Option Nat

/-- Place of the minimal kernel: allocation identity, offset and length (§11 ¶1). -/
structure Place where
  alloc : Nat
  off : Nat
  len : Nat

/-- Means of access: address, provenance (an allocation identity), length and elementary
access authority (§12 ¶1, §12 ¶2). -/
structure Access where
  addr : Nat
  prov : Nat
  len : Nat
  auth : Auth

/-- Abstract state: registered allocations by identity, live or dead, and the counter `next`
representing the freshness discipline (§9 ¶7, §13 ¶1). -/
structure State where
  allocs : Nat → Option Alloc
  next : Nat

/-- Well-formedness of identities and freshness: no identity at or above the counter is
registered (§9 ¶7, §9 ¶8 b1). -/
def WF (s : State) : Prop := ∀ i, s.next ≤ i → s.allocs i = none

/-- Spatial containment of an access in an allocation (§15 ¶1; used by §15.2 and §16.2). -/
def Spatial (a : Alloc) (ac : Access) : Prop :=
  a.base ≤ ac.addr ∧ ac.addr + ac.len ≤ a.base + a.size

/-- Spatial containment is decidable (§15 ¶1). -/
instance (a : Alloc) (ac : Access) : Decidable (Spatial a ac) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (a.base ≤ ac.addr ∧ ac.addr + ac.len ≤ a.base + a.size))

/-- The `len` bytes from offset `off` are initialized (§15.3, read as: every byte of the
accessed range). -/
def Alloc.InitRange (a : Alloc) (off len : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, i < len → a.bytes (off + i) ≠ .uninit

/-- Initialization of a range is decidable (§15.3). -/
instance (a : Alloc) (off len : Nat) : Decidable (a.InitRange off len) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ i, i < len → a.bytes (off + i) ≠ .uninit))

/-- Kernel conditions of a raw typed read by `ac`: §15.1, §15.2, §15.3 and §15.5. The
conditions §15.4, §15.6 and §15.7 are the parametric obligations of `ReadOblSpec`. -/
def CanRead (s : State) (ac : Access) : Prop :=
  ∃ a, s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ a.live = true ∧ Spatial a ac ∧
    a.InitRange (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len ∧ Auth.read ≤ ac.auth

/-- Kernel conditions of a raw typed write by `ac`: §16.1, §16.2 and §16.3. The conditions
§16.4–§16.6 are the parametric obligations of `WriteOblSpec`. -/
def CanWrite (s : State) (ac : Access) : Prop :=
  ∃ a, s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ a.live = true ∧ Spatial a ac ∧ Auth.write ≤ ac.auth

/-- The kernel conditions of a read are decidable (§15). -/
instance (s : State) (ac : Access) : Decidable (CanRead s ac) :=
  match h : s.allocs ac.prov with
  | some a =>
    if hc : a.live = true ∧ Spatial a ac ∧ a.InitRange (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len ∧
        Auth.read ≤ ac.auth then isTrue ⟨a, h, hc⟩
    else isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, hb'⟩ => hc (by rw [h] at hb; cases hb; exact hb')
  | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _⟩ => by rw [h] at hb; cases hb

/-- The kernel conditions of a write are decidable (§16). -/
instance (s : State) (ac : Access) : Decidable (CanWrite s ac) :=
  match h : s.allocs ac.prov with
  | some a =>
    if hc : a.live = true ∧ Spatial a ac ∧ Auth.write ≤ ac.auth then isTrue ⟨a, h, hc⟩
    else isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, hb'⟩ => hc (by rw [h] at hb; cases hb; exact hb')
  | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _⟩ => by rw [h] at hb; cases hb

/-- Partial resolution of a means of access to a place (§11 ¶2): defined when the
provenance identifies a registered allocation, live or dead, that spatially contains the
access. It proves no right to read or write. -/
def Access.toPlace (s : State) (ac : Access) : Option Place :=
  match s.allocs ac.prov with
  | some a => if Spatial a ac then some ⟨ac.prov, ac.addr - a.base, ac.len⟩ else none
  | none => none

/-- Characterization of resolution (§11 ¶2). -/
theorem toPlace_eq_some {s : State} {ac : Access} {p : Place} :
    ac.toPlace s = some p ↔
      ∃ a, s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ Spatial a ac ∧
        p = ⟨ac.prov, ac.addr - a.base, ac.len⟩ := by
  unfold Access.toPlace
  split
  · next a ha =>
    by_cases hs : Spatial a ac
    · simp [hs, ha, eq_comm]
    · simp [hs, ha]
  · next ha => simp [ha]

/-- The `len` bytes of `a` from offset `off`: the value of a valid read (§20.2 ¶1). -/
def Alloc.bytesAt (a : Alloc) (off len : Nat) : List AByte :=
  (List.range len).map fun i => a.bytes (off + i)

/-- The `len` written bytes from position `off` of the supplied representation `w`, each
initialized with its value and provenance (§16 ¶2, §16 ¶5). -/
def writtenBytes (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (off len : Nat) : List AByte :=
  (List.range len).map fun i => .init (w (off + i)).1 (w (off + i)).2

/-- Effect of a valid write on storage (§16 ¶2, §10 ¶4): the bytes at offsets
`[off, off + len)` are replaced byte by byte by `w`, initialized with the supplied value and
provenance; other bytes are unchanged (§16 ¶3). -/
def Alloc.write (a : Alloc) (off len : Nat) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) : Alloc :=
  { a with bytes := fun j =>
      if off ≤ j ∧ j < off + len then .init (w (j - off)).1 (w (j - off)).2 else a.bytes j }

/-- Effect of a valid write of `w` through `ac` on the state (§16 ¶2, §16 ¶3). -/
def State.write (s : State) (ac : Access) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) : State :=
  { s with allocs := fun i =>
      if i = ac.prov then (s.allocs i).map (fun a => a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w)
      else s.allocs i }

/-- Conditions of a successful raw deallocation of `id` with presented authority `auth`
(§17.1, §17.2): live, deallocatable, and `auth` compatible with the recorded token under the
context relation `C` (§17 ¶2, §17 ¶4). -/
def CanDealloc (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (s : State) (id auth : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ a, s.allocs id = some a ∧ a.live = true ∧ ∃ d, a.freeAuth = some d ∧ C auth d

/-- Deallocation conditions are decidable when compatibility is (§17, §20.3 ¶3). -/
instance {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} [DecidableRel C] (s : State) (id auth : Nat) :
    Decidable (CanDealloc C s id auth) :=
  match h : s.allocs id with
  | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _⟩ => by rw [h] at hb; cases hb
  | some a =>
    match hf : a.freeAuth with
    | none => isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, _, d, hd, _⟩ => by
        rw [h] at hb
        cases hb
        rw [hf] at hd
        cases hd
    | some d =>
      if hc : a.live = true ∧ C auth d then isTrue ⟨a, h, hc.1, d, hf, hc.2⟩
      else isFalse fun ⟨b, hb, hl, d', hd', hc'⟩ => hc (by
        rw [h] at hb
        cases hb
        rw [hf] at hd'
        cases hd'
        exact ⟨hl, hc'⟩)

/-- Effect of a valid deallocation (§17 ¶3, §20.2 ¶2): `id` becomes dead and stays
registered (§13 ¶1). -/
def State.dealloc (s : State) (id : Nat) : State :=
  { s with allocs := fun i =>
      if i = id then (s.allocs i).map (fun a => { a with live := false }) else s.allocs i }

/-- Effect of a valid raw creation (§9 ¶11, §13 ¶1, §20.2 ¶2): a live allocation under the
identity `s.next`, wholly uninitialized (§10 ¶5); the counter advances (§9 ¶7). -/
def State.alloc (s : State) (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat) : State :=
  { allocs := fun i =>
      if i = s.next then
        some { space, base, size, align, live := true, bytes := fun _ => .uninit, freeAuth }
      else s.allocs i
    next := s.next + 1 }

/-- Half-open ranges `[b1, b1 + n1)` and `[b2, b2 + n2)` have an empty intersection (§9 ¶3). -/
def RangeDisjoint (b1 n1 b2 n2 : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, b1 ≤ x → x < b1 + n1 → b2 ≤ x → x < b2 + n2 → False

/-- Arithmetic form of range disjointness (§9 ¶3). -/
theorem rangeDisjoint_iff {b1 n1 b2 n2 : Nat} :
    RangeDisjoint b1 n1 b2 n2 ↔ b1 + n1 ≤ b2 ∨ b2 + n2 ≤ b1 ∨ n1 = 0 ∨ n2 = 0 := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    rcases Nat.le_total b1 b2 with h12 | h12
    · by_cases hlt : b2 < b1 + n1
      · by_cases hn : 0 < n2
        · exact (h b2 h12 hlt (Nat.le_refl _) (by omega)).elim
        · omega
      · omega
    · by_cases hlt : b1 < b2 + n2
      · by_cases hn : 0 < n1
        · exact (h b1 (Nat.le_refl _) (by omega) h12 hlt).elim
        · omega
      · omega
  · intro h x h1 h2 h3 h4
    omega

/-- Range disjointness is decidable (§9 ¶3). -/
instance (b1 n1 b2 n2 : Nat) : Decidable (RangeDisjoint b1 n1 b2 n2) :=
  decidable_of_iff _ rangeDisjoint_iff.symm

/-- Disjointness of live allocations in the same address space (§9 ¶3, §9 ¶8 b2). -/
def LiveDisjoint (s : State) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j a b, i ≠ j → s.allocs i = some a → s.allocs j = some b →
    a.live = true → b.live = true → a.space = b.space →
    RangeDisjoint a.base a.size b.base b.size

/-- `n` is a power of two (§9 ¶1 b5, §9 ¶4). -/
def Pow2 (n : Nat) : Prop := ∃ k, n = 2 ^ k

/-- Bounded form of `Pow2` (§9 ¶4). -/
theorem pow2_iff (n : Nat) : Pow2 n ↔ ∃ k, k < n + 1 ∧ n = 2 ^ k :=
  ⟨fun ⟨k, hk⟩ => ⟨k, by have := @Nat.lt_two_pow_self k; omega, hk⟩, fun ⟨k, _, hk⟩ => ⟨k, hk⟩⟩

/-- `Pow2` is decidable (§9 ¶4). -/
instance (n : Nat) : Decidable (Pow2 n) :=
  decidable_of_iff _ (pow2_iff n).symm

/-- Operation preconditions of raw creation in space `space` (§9 ¶11): fresh identity
`s.next`, strictly positive power-of-two alignment, aligned base, no overlap with any live
allocation of the same space. -/
def AllocPre (s : State) (space base size align : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.allocs s.next = none ∧ 0 < align ∧ Pow2 align ∧ base % align = 0 ∧
    ∀ i a, s.allocs i = some a → a.live = true → a.space = space →
      RangeDisjoint a.base a.size base size

/-- The entry `o` does not overlap `[base, base + size)` in space `space`: absent, dead, of
another space, or disjoint (§9 ¶11). -/
def NoOverlap (space base size : Nat) : Option Alloc → Prop
  | some a => a.live = true → a.space = space → RangeDisjoint a.base a.size base size
  | none => True

/-- `NoOverlap` is decidable (§9 ¶11). -/
instance (space base size : Nat) : (o : Option Alloc) → Decidable (NoOverlap space base size o)
  | some a => inferInstanceAs
      (Decidable (a.live = true → a.space = space → RangeDisjoint a.base a.size base size))
  | none => inferInstanceAs (Decidable True)

/-- Decidable form of `AllocPre`, checking overlap on identities below the counter only
(§9 ¶11, §20.3 ¶3). -/
def AllocPreDec (s : State) (space base size align : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.allocs s.next = none ∧ 0 < align ∧ Pow2 align ∧ base % align = 0 ∧
    ∀ i, i < s.next → NoOverlap space base size (s.allocs i)

/-- `AllocPreDec` is decidable (§20.3 ¶3). -/
instance (s : State) (space base size align : Nat) :
    Decidable (AllocPreDec s space base size align) := by
  unfold AllocPreDec
  infer_instance

/-- Under freshness, `AllocPreDec` is `AllocPre` (§9 ¶7, §9 ¶11). -/
theorem allocPreDec_iff {s : State} (hwf : WF s) {space base size align : Nat} :
    AllocPreDec s space base size align ↔ AllocPre s space base size align := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hf, h0, h2, hm, hd⟩
    refine ⟨hf, h0, h2, hm, fun i a ha hl hsp => ?_⟩
    have hi : i < s.next := Nat.lt_of_not_le fun hle => by rw [hwf i hle] at ha; cases ha
    have := hd i hi
    rw [ha] at this
    exact this hl hsp
  · rintro ⟨hf, h0, h2, hm, hd⟩
    refine ⟨hf, h0, h2, hm, fun i _ => ?_⟩
    cases ha : s.allocs i with
    | none => trivial
    | some a => exact fun hl hsp => hd i a ha hl hsp

/-- Alignment of every registered allocation, live or dead (§9 ¶4, §9 ¶8 b3). -/
def Aligned (s : State) : Prop :=
  ∀ i a, s.allocs i = some a → 0 < a.align ∧ Pow2 a.align ∧ a.base % a.align = 0

/-- Admissible state (§9 ¶8): freshness, live disjointness, alignment. -/
structure Admissible (s : State) : Prop where
  wf : WF s
  disjoint : LiveDisjoint s
  aligned : Aligned s

/-- The empty state: no allocation, counter `0` (§9 ¶9). -/
def State.empty : State := ⟨fun _ => none, 0⟩

/-- The empty state is an admissible initial state (§9 ¶9). -/
theorem admissible_empty : Admissible State.empty :=
  ⟨fun _ _ => rfl, (fun _ _ _ _ _ h => nomatch h), (fun _ _ h => nomatch h)⟩

/-! ## Restrictive derivation (§14) -/

/-- `ac'` is a restrictive derivation of `ac` (§14 ¶1): same provenance, address subrange,
authority at most that of the source. -/
def Derive (ac ac' : Access) : Prop :=
  ac.addr ≤ ac'.addr ∧ ac'.addr + ac'.len ≤ ac.addr + ac.len ∧
    ac'.prov = ac.prov ∧ ac'.auth ≤ ac.auth

/-- A restrictive derivation preserves provenance (§14 ¶1 b1). -/
theorem derive_prov {ac ac' : Access} (hd : Derive ac ac') : ac'.prov = ac.prov :=
  hd.2.2.1

/-- A restrictive derivation of an access contained in an allocation is contained in it
(§14 ¶1 b2, §15 ¶1). -/
theorem derive_spatial {ac ac' : Access} (hd : Derive ac ac') {a : Alloc}
    (hs : Spatial a ac) : Spatial a ac' := by
  obtain ⟨h1, h2, -, -⟩ := hd
  obtain ⟨h3, h4⟩ := hs
  exact ⟨Nat.le_trans h3 h1, Nat.le_trans h2 h4⟩

/-- A restrictive derivation confers no greater authority (§14 ¶1 b3). -/
theorem derive_auth_le {ac ac' : Access} (hd : Derive ac ac') : ac'.auth ≤ ac.auth :=
  hd.2.2.2

/-! ## Parametric obligations and outcomes (§15 ¶5, §16 ¶4, §20) -/

/-- Read obligations not defined by the kernel, §15.4, §15.6, §15.7 (§15 ¶5): explicit
predicates of the execution context (§20.3 ¶1), depending on the state, the access and the
read type; `dec` is the part with a decision procedure, `stat` the part established
statically or by contract (§20.3 ¶2). -/
structure ReadOblSpec (Ty : Type) where
  dec : State → Access → Ty → Prop
  stat : State → Access → Ty → Prop

/-- Read obligations with a decision instance for `dec`, as required by a computable
interpreter (§20.3 ¶3). -/
structure ReadObl (Ty : Type) extends toSpec : ReadOblSpec Ty where
  decInst : ∀ s ac t, Decidable (dec s ac t)

attribute [instance] ReadObl.decInst

/-- Write obligations not defined by the kernel, §16.4, §16.5, §16.6 (§16 ¶4): explicit
predicates of the execution context (§20.3 ¶1), depending on the state, the access, the
written type and the supplied representation; split into `dec` and `stat` (§20.3 ¶2). -/
structure WriteOblSpec (Ty : Type) where
  dec : State → Access → Ty → (Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) → Prop
  stat : State → Access → Ty → (Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) → Prop

/-- Write obligations with a decision instance for `dec`, as required by a computable
interpreter (§20.3 ¶3). -/
structure WriteObl (Ty : Type) extends toSpec : WriteOblSpec Ty where
  decInst : ∀ s ac t w, Decidable (dec s ac t w)

attribute [instance] WriteObl.decInst

/-- Outcome of a raw state-transforming operation: `ok` with the new state, or `ub`, which
supplies no state (§20.1 ¶2, §1). -/
inductive Outcome where
  | ok (s : State)
  | ub

/-- Outcome of a raw read: `ok` with the bytes read, or `ub` (§20.1 ¶2, §20.2 ¶1). -/
inductive ReadOutcome where
  | ok (v : List AByte)
  | ub
  deriving DecidableEq

section Relations

variable {Ty : Type}

/-- Raw typed read of type `t` through `ac` (§15, §20.1, §20.2 ¶1): `ok` with the bytes of
the accessed range when the kernel conditions (`CanRead`) and both parts of the obligations
hold; `ub` otherwise, a violated static part included (§20.1 ¶2 b2). The state is
unchanged. -/
inductive ReadStep (ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty) (s : State) :
    ReadOutcome → Prop where
  | ok {a : Alloc} : s.allocs ac.prov = some a → CanRead s ac ∧ ObR.dec s ac t ∧ ObR.stat s ac t →
      ReadStep ObR ac t s (.ok (a.bytesAt (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len))
  | ub : ¬ (CanRead s ac ∧ ObR.dec s ac t ∧ ObR.stat s ac t) → ReadStep ObR ac t s .ub

/-- Raw typed write of `w` at type `t` through `ac` (§16, §20.1, §20.2 ¶2): `ok` with the
effect `State.write` when the kernel conditions (`CanWrite`) and both parts of the
obligations hold; `ub` otherwise (§20.1 ¶2 b2). -/
inductive WriteStep (ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty)
    (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (s : State) : Outcome → Prop where
  | ok : CanWrite s ac ∧ ObW.dec s ac t w ∧ ObW.stat s ac t w →
      WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok (s.write ac w))
  | ub : ¬ (CanWrite s ac ∧ ObW.dec s ac t w ∧ ObW.stat s ac t w) → WriteStep ObW ac t w s .ub

end Relations

/-- Raw deallocation of `id` with presented authority `auth` (§17, §20.1, §20.2 ¶2): `ok`
with the effect `State.dealloc` when `CanDealloc`; `ub` otherwise. `C` needs no decision
instance (§20.3 ¶3). -/
inductive DeallocStep (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (id auth : Nat) (s : State) : Outcome → Prop where
  | ok : CanDealloc C s id auth → DeallocStep C id auth s (.ok (s.dealloc id))
  | ub : ¬ CanDealloc C s id auth → DeallocStep C id auth s .ub

/-- Raw creation (§9 ¶11, §20.1, §20.2 ¶2): `ok` with the effect `State.alloc` when
`AllocPre`; `ub` otherwise. -/
inductive AllocStep (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat) (s : State) :
    Outcome → Prop where
  | ok : AllocPre s space base size align →
      AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s (.ok (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth))
  | ub : ¬ AllocPre s space base size align → AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s .ub

/-! ## Interpreters (§20.3 ¶3; `formal/DESIGN.md`, "Representation") -/

section Interpreters

variable {Ty : Type}

/-- Interpreter of `ReadStep`: decides the kernel conditions and `dec`, takes the static
part `stat` as a proof argument (§20.3 ¶3), and returns the bytes read (§20.2 ¶1). -/
def read (ObR : ReadObl Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty) (s : State) (_hs : ObR.stat s ac t) :
    ReadOutcome :=
  match s.allocs ac.prov with
  | some a =>
    if CanRead s ac ∧ ObR.dec s ac t then .ok (a.bytesAt (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len) else .ub
  | none => .ub

/-- Interpreter of `WriteStep`: decides the kernel conditions and `dec`, takes `stat` as a
proof argument (§20.3 ¶3). -/
def write (ObW : WriteObl Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (s : State)
    (_hs : ObW.stat s ac t w) : Outcome :=
  if CanWrite s ac ∧ ObW.dec s ac t w then .ok (s.write ac w) else .ub

end Interpreters

/-- Interpreter of `DeallocStep`, given a decision instance for compatibility (§20.3 ¶3). -/
def dealloc (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) [DecidableRel C] (id auth : Nat) (s : State) : Outcome :=
  if CanDealloc C s id auth then .ok (s.dealloc id) else .ub

/-- Interpreter of `AllocStep`, taking freshness `WF s` as a proof argument; it decides
`AllocPreDec`, which is `AllocPre` under `WF` (§9 ¶11, §20.3 ¶3). -/
def alloc (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat) (s : State) (_hwf : WF s) :
    Outcome :=
  if AllocPreDec s space base size align then .ok (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth)
  else .ub

/-! ## Executions (§9 ¶9, §20.1 ¶2, §20.3 ¶3) -/

/-- Raw operations of the machine (§15, §16, §17, §9 ¶11, §20.1). -/
inductive Op (Ty : Type) where
  | read (ac : Access) (t : Ty)
  | write (ac : Access) (t : Ty) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat)
  | dealloc (id auth : Nat)
  | alloc (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat)

section Executions

variable {Ty : Type}

/-- `ok` transitions of the raw operations, with compatibility and obligations fixed by the
execution context (§20.1 ¶2, §20.3 ¶3). A read leaves the state unchanged (§20.2 ¶1). -/
inductive Step (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty) :
    Op Ty → State → State → Prop where
  | read {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State} {v : List AByte} :
      ReadStep ObR ac t s (.ok v) → Step C ObR ObW (.read ac t) s s
  | write {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s' : State} :
      WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s') → Step C ObR ObW (.write ac t w) s s'
  | dealloc {id auth : Nat} {s s' : State} :
      DeallocStep C id auth s (.ok s') → Step C ObR ObW (.dealloc id auth) s s'
  | alloc {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat} {s s' : State} :
      AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s (.ok s') →
      Step C ObR ObW (.alloc space base size align freeAuth) s s'

/-- Execution: a sequence of `ok` steps under one context (§20.3 ¶3). A `ub` step supplies
no state, so it never occurs inside an execution (§20.1 ¶2 b3). -/
inductive Exec (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty) :
    List (Op Ty) → State → State → Prop where
  | nil (s : State) : Exec C ObR ObW [] s s
  | cons {op : Op Ty} {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s s' s'' : State} :
      Step C ObR ObW op s s' → Exec C ObR ObW ops s' s'' → Exec C ObR ObW (op :: ops) s s''

/-- `s` is reachable from the initial state `s₀`, which need not be empty (§9 ¶9). -/
def Reachable (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty)
    (s₀ s : State) : Prop :=
  ∃ ops, Exec C ObR ObW ops s₀ s

/-- The operation neither writes through provenance `i` nor deallocates `i`. Used to state
the "absence of an intervening write or invalidation" of §16 ¶5 for allocation `i`; writes
through other provenances are allowed (non-interference, §16 ¶5). -/
def Op.KeepsAlloc (i : Nat) : Op Ty → Prop
  | .read _ _ => True
  | .write ac _ _ => ac.prov ≠ i
  | .dealloc id _ => id ≠ i
  | .alloc .. => True

end Executions

theorem WriteStep_ok_iff {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}

    WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s') ↔
      (CanWrite s ac ∧ ObW.dec s ac t w ∧ ObW.stat s ac t w) ∧ s' = s.write ac w :=
  ⟨fun h => by cases h with | ok h => exact ⟨h, rfl⟩, fun ⟨h, e⟩ => by subst e; exact .ok h⟩

/-- `ok` outcome of a raw deallocation (§17, §20.1 ¶2 b1). -/
theorem DeallocStep_ok_iff {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {id auth : Nat} {s s' : State} :
    DeallocStep C id auth s (.ok s') ↔ CanDealloc C s id auth ∧ s' = s.dealloc id :=
  ⟨fun h => by cases h with | ok h => exact ⟨h, rfl⟩, fun ⟨h, e⟩ => by subst e; exact .ok h⟩

/-- A raw read has at most one outcome (§20.1 ¶3). -/
theorem ReadStep_det {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State}
    {o₁ o₂ : ReadOutcome} (h₁ : ReadStep ObR ac t s o₁) (h₂ : ReadStep ObR ac t s o₂) :
    o₁ = o₂ := by
  cases h₁ with
  | ok ha _ =>
    cases h₂ with
    | ok hb _ => rw [ha] at hb; cases hb; rfl
    | ub => contradiction
  | ub => cases h₂ with
    | ok => contradiction
    | ub => rfl

theorem WriteStep_det {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s : State} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome}
    (h₁ : WriteStep ObW ac t w s o₁) (h₂ : WriteStep ObW ac t w s o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := by
  cases h₁ <;> cases h₂ <;> first | rfl | contradiction

theorem ReadStep_total (ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty) (ac : Access) (t : Ty) (s : State) :
    ¬¬ ∃ o, ReadStep ObR ac t s o :=

  fun hn => hn ⟨.ub, .ub fun h => hn ⟨_, .ok h⟩⟩

theorem AllocStep_total (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat) (s : State) :
